title: Scalable likelihood-based inference for limited dependent variable models
abstract: arXiv:2608.13851v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Limited dependent variable models are central to empirical economics, but likelihood-based inference is infeasible when likelihoods involve high-dimensional integration over latent variables. This paper proposes Stochastically Estimated Gradient Ascent (SEGA), a scalable estimation approach for limited dependent variable models. Using Fisher's identity, SEGA replaces the intractable likelihood score with an unbiased augmented-data score evaluated at a single conditional draw of the latent variables, and embeds this score in a stochastic gradient ascent algorithm. With sufficiently many iterations, we show that SEGA is asymptotically equivalent to the infeasible maximum likelihood estimator. A variance estimator based on Fisher's and Louis' identities is proposed that allows inference to proceed in the usual manner. Applications to brand choice and household demand demonstrate the usefulness of SEGA for conducting inference in large-scale

translated_title: 有限因变量模型的可扩展似然推断方法
translated_abstract: 有限因变量模型是实证经济学的核心，但当似然函数涉及对潜变量的高维积分时，基于似然的推断变得不可行。本文提出了一种随机估计梯度上升（SEGA）方法，这是一种用于有限因变量模型的可扩展估计方法。利用Fisher恒等式，SEGA用潜变量单次条件抽样下的无偏增广数据得分替换了难以处理的似然得分，并将该得分嵌入随机梯度上升算法中。在足够多的迭代下，我们证明SEGA与不可行的最大似然估计渐近等价。基于Fisher和Louis恒等式的方差估计器被提出，使得推断能以常规方式进行。应用于品牌选择和家庭需求的案例展示了SEGA在大规模推断中的实用性。
tldr: 本文提出SEGA方法，通过随机梯度上升和Fisher恒等式，使有限因变量模型的高维似然推断变得可扩展且渐近等价于最大似然估计。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SEGA, a scalable method using stochastic gradient ascent and Fisher's identity, making high-dimensional likelihood inference for limited dependent variable models feasible and asymptotically equivalent to maximum likelihood estimation.
